answer.evidence: The upper band (rows 1-17) is a wide roof surface with a roof vent (rows 7-10) and a skylight, and the cab windshield sits at the east end. Row 17 is a darker line across the body, which I read as the front-edge line, with lighter rows 18-19 just below it. Below that, rows 18-28 are the south face with a sliding-door outline and rust, and the tyres extend to row 30. This is a reading of an ambiguous drawing: the band could be taken as a side elevation with windows. The roof vent and the dividing line at row 17 favour a roof plane over a front face. No eave shadow is clearly visible.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate carries 13 visible tones per full tile, between the hedge (9) and the cheese stall and well (17-20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. The roof panel shows about 5 grey-blue steps, with rust patches in several orange-brown tones, streaks and speckle, a lighter panel edge, a dark window and tyres. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans tinted (dark brown-grey), not a uniform black sticker line. The van is separated by value and rust variation, which fits how the references use dark material tones selectively. Texture and density are comparable to the stall and well references, and the style matches the Beodeul standard.
